bull.t: Data Center Growth and Market Position
bull.b: Data Center is already Marvell’s dominant revenue engine, and sustained high growth expectations indicate strong exposure to expanding AI infrastructure, networking and connectivity demand. This scale can reinforce design wins and improve operating leverage over time.

The rebound to strong margins and positive free cash flow demonstrates meaningful earnings power at current scale. If sustained through the growth cycle, this profitability can fund research, capacity commitments and shareholder returns without relying heavily on external financing.

Custom silicon programs and high-speed connectivity products can create multi-year customer relationships, engineering barriers and recurring production volumes. Broader product adoption, including hyperscaler engagement, strengthens Marvell’s strategic role in infrastructure platforms.

bear.b: Recent losses show that Marvell remains exposed to semiconductor demand cycles, customer inventory adjustments and infrastructure spending changes. Sustaining the current earnings profile is therefore important; a downturn could materially weaken margins and returns.

Large supplier prepayments and elevated inventory support expansion but absorb cash before corresponding revenue is realized. Combined with cash flow below net income, this increases working-capital risk and could reduce financial flexibility if demand or ramps slow.

The communications business remains uneven, while rapid custom growth can dilute margins before scale benefits emerge. This mix sensitivity may make consolidated results more variable and complicate execution even as Data Center demand expands.
